document_title: Drawn to Scale, Except the Demand
post_copy:
One column tallies 119.7 megawatts becoming 120.0. The other tallies about 4,700 acres. No unit joins them.

The megawatts are Bradley Lake. The Alaska Energy Authority has asked FERC to divert Dixon Glacier meltwater into the lake and add a 0.3 MW turbine. AEA projects about 38 percent more average annual generation. More water, not more hardware. Comments close 28 August at 5:00 p.m. Eastern.

The acres are twelve Air Force parcels at JBER, Eielson and Clear, offered for AI data centers. Robert Moriarty cited "the growing demands of the AI industry."

That offer names no megawatts. No published number bridges the two records.

Slides carry the fishwater valve in section, the capacity bar against the generation bar, and the twelve parcels.

So is that blank a hole in the record, or just not the Air Force's number to publish?

#Railbelt #DixonDiversion #AlaskaEnergy

Sources for today's deck, in the order the claims appear.

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, notice of application accepted for filing, Federal Register 2026-08-03, docket P-8221-124 -- https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-03/html/2026-15691.htm

Federal Register API record for the same notice, 2026-08-03 -- https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents/2026-15691.json

Alaska Energy Authority, Dixon Diversion Project page (cost, schedule, siting) -- https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project/Dixon-Diversion-Project

Alaska Energy Authority, Bradley Lake Hydroelectric Project page (392,000 MWh 1995 to 2020 average, about 10 percent of Railbelt annual power) -- https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Bradley-Lake-Hydroelectric-Project

Alaska Energy Authority newsroom, board endorses a financing package, 2026-07-23 -- https://www.akenergyauthority.org/Who-We-Are/Newsroom/Press-Releases

Petroleum News, Alan Bailey, 2026-08-02 (the 4.6 mile tunnel, up to 30,000 homes) -- https://www.petroleumnews.com/story/2026/08/02/news/aea-final-amendment-application-for-bradley-lake-filed-with-ferc/50288.html

U.S. Department of the Air Force, 2026-04-10 (about 4,700 acres, twelve parcels, the Moriarty quotation) -- https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/

HigherGov mirror of SAM.gov solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006, last updated 2026-07-14 -- https://www.highergov.com/contract-opportunity/rflp-artificial-intelligence-ai-data-center-deve-afcec-26-r-0006-o-db695/

One number on slide 07 is ours, not anyone else's. About 149,000 megawatt hours a year is 38 percent applied to the 392,000 MWh average. Nobody has published an absolute figure for the expansion, and the slide says so.

Nothing in the Bradley Lake record mentions AI or data centres, and the Air Force offer names no megawatts. The deck does not connect them and neither does any document we found.
